The same finding, months apart, is two different conversations.

A dealer starts writing business that looks ordinary. Several months later the claims on that book are arriving well above what those contracts were priced for.

Found as it forms, that is a phone call. Here is what we are seeing, here is what is driving it, here is what we would like to do about it. The dealer is a participant. Something can still change.

Found at reconciliation, it is a different call entirely. The exposure is written. The losses are developing. The conversation is about attribution rather than action, and everybody in it is reacting.

Same dealer. Same numbers. The only variable is when.

Periodic reporting answers what the book looked like when the cycle ran, and answers it well. It was never built to tell you the month a pattern stopped being noise. That is a different question, and it is the one this is built for.

Watch

It reads the whole book, every cycle, and tells you what deserves a look.

Every dealer, every product, measured against what those specific contracts were priced to cost. Nothing is sampled, and nothing waits for somebody to run a report.

Not every deviation becomes a finding. Three things have to be true at once before anything reaches a person: enough claims to judge it, a gap beyond ordinary variation, and a gap large enough to matter. What clears all three is actionable; what clears a lower bar is advisory. A subject that is behaving is reported as behaving, not left out — silence you cannot audit is indistinguishable from a blind spot.

None of this needs a systems project. It runs on the contract, claim and cancellation records you already produce — which is also why you can see what it would have found on your own book before committing to anything.

Found as it happens

Eight quiet months, one warning, then it crossed.

The same dealer, replayed at each of the last twelve months — every verdict computed using only the data that existed at that point, with everything after it hidden.

This is the difference the product is actually selling. Not a cleverer report at quarter end: a verdict that changes month by month as the evidence accumulates, and says so the month it changes.

Observation point

Drag it back. Everything after the month you land on disappears, because that is what the watch could see at the time. The verdict is the one it would have reached that month.

Two things are worth noticing. The system stayed silent through eight months of ordinary variation, which is what makes the ninth month mean something. And the first signal was an advisory, not an alarm — a month of warning before anything was worth acting on.

Investigate

Open the finding and the work is already done.

The comparison is against your own expectations, not a benchmark. The expected line is built from your pricing assumptions, contract by contract, each at its own age — so a dealer's own mix is already inside it.

Which is why "they just sell riskier vehicles" stops being an explanation. It was accounted for before anybody asked.

That last line is the kind of thing a report written to justify itself would leave out. The finding is worth less if you act on the wrong half of it.

From there, slice it however you suspect — by product, vehicle class, mileage band, repair facility, agency, F&I desk, adjuster decision. Follow the questions the system raises, or ask your own in plain English.

Decide

Then: here is what is worth doing about it.

The actions your business has already sanctioned, ranked — each with what it costs, how fast it acts, whether it can be undone, and what it cannot fix.

One is recommended, with the reasoning shown. A person decides. Nothing executes anywhere.

Every option names its limit. Re-pricing fixes new business and cannot touch the in-force book. Tightening terms is the fastest brake and costs the most relationship. Doing nothing for one more cycle is a real choice with a real price on it.

AI does the reading. The arithmetic is arithmetic.

The AI reads your contracts and claims, works through the dimensions, explains what is driving a finding, and recommends an action. The numbers underneath are computed deterministically — the same book produces the same answer every time, and every figure traces back to the contracts and claims behind it.

The product states its own boundary, on the screen, permanently: the model translates your question and narrates the result. It never calculates. With generation switched off, the finding is identical.

That is the difference between an answer you can act on and one you have to check. An underwriting position has to survive a carrier, a client and an auditor.

And the reasoning is kept. What was known at the time, what was decided, what was rejected and why. The next time the question comes up, the answer starts from a record rather than somebody's memory.

So you can ask it things. Not a search box over documents — the question becomes a query the page runs, and the answer is the page.

It also names its own limits, on the screen, without being asked. These three are quoted from the panel that sits under every finding:

“Every measure on this screen is computed over this trailing window. A deviation that began earlier and has since settled will not appear.”

“These assumptions were taken as given. Nothing here was screened for thinness or for being indistinguishable from its parent — those are checks on a basis we fit ourselves, and this one we did not.”

“The assumptions are stored exactly as supplied and are never refit. A new version number would mean the customer supplied different assumptions, not that anything was recalculated.”

The evaluation

See what your own book would have told you.

You don't have to take any of this on trust. Send a historical extract. We build your expectation from your own pricing assumptions, then replay the book as it stood at each past month — using only what was knowable then.

What would it have found?

When would it have found it?

Why did it matter?

And what actually happened next. It is your book, so every finding can be checked against what you already know.

For the evaluation: one file. No integration, no connection to your systems, nothing installed. De-identify it before it leaves you — hash the dealer, contract and vehicle identifiers on your side and keep the key. This is a book of numbers and dates; it does not need to say who anyone is.

For production, the system needs the book kept current — but that is a data feed, not a systems project. A scheduled export of files you already produce is enough.
